newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - US fundamentals speak for higher dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - US fundamentals speak for higher dollar.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, in an interview with a German news agency, said U.S. economic fundamentals should allow the dollar to be stronger.
"In my view the economic fundamental data in the United States would speak for the dollar to be valued at a slightly higher rate," Tietmeyer said.
A Bundesbank spokesman confirmed the quote to Reuters in answer to an enquiry.
The dollar rose after Tietmeyer's comments were confirmed to Reuters, rising to about 1.4830 marks from about the level of 1.4805 marks.
The Bundesbank has long supported the idea of a strong dollar, saying a stronger mark was slightly negative for the economy and would dampen Germany's exports.
Germany's fledgling economic recovery ground to a temporary halt last spring when the mark appreciated strongly against many European currencies and the dollar.
